newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's FO union seeks minimum wage rise.
newsitem.headline: France's FO union seeks minimum wage rise.

text.p: The head of the Force Ouvriere union, Marc Blondel, said on Wednesday he asked Prime Minister Lionel Jospin for an increase in the monthly minimum wage of 400 to 500 francs, representing a rise of 6.2 to 7.8 percent.
"We expect a significant increase in the minimum wage on the order of 400 to 500 francs, or 6.2 to 7.8 percent," he said in a statement issued after a meeting with Jospin.
The statement did not say whether the increase would be immediate or staggered.

The Communist-led CGT is pushing hard for a large rise in the minimum wage, but to date the FO and the large CFDT unions had said they favoured a rise but had also warned against too big an increase on the grounds that minimum wage earners get relief on contributions needed for the social security system.
The monthly minimum wage stands at 6,406.79 francs a month.
